pages.text: Today I am going to get my hair cut.
First, my grown-up and I will travel to the hairdresser.
I will wait in the waiting area. There might be other people there.
When it is my turn, the hairdresser will show me the special chair.
The hairdresser might wash my hair first. The water is usually warm. If it feels too hot or too cold, I can tell the hairdresser.
The hairdresser uses scissors to cut my hair. Keeping my head still helps the hairdresser cut safely. If I need a break, I can say 'stop, please'.
I can look in the mirror to see my new haircut.
When the haircut is finished, we can go home. I can tell my grown-up how it felt.
Today we are going to the supermarket to buy food.
We will drive to the supermarket together.
We have a list of things we need to buy.
I can help push the trolley through the shop.
We will put the food into the trolley as we go around.
Sometimes the shop has run out of something. That is OK, we can choose something else.
At the end we pay for our food at the checkout.
When we have paid, we can go home.
Today I am going to travel on the bus.
I will wait at the bus stop. The bus usually comes soon. Sometimes it is late, and the sign at the stop might show how long it will be.
I will need my bus pass or money for the fare.
When the bus stops, people getting off usually go first. Then it is our turn to get on.
If there is a free seat, I can sit down. If the bus is full, I can hold on to a pole or handle.
Many people on the bus talk quietly. Staying in my seat while the bus moves helps keep me safe.
When my stop is coming up, I can press the bell to tell the driver.
When we get to my stop, I get off the bus. I can tell my grown-up how the journey went.
When the clock says bedtime, I start getting ready for sleep.
First I have a bath or shower to get clean.
Then I brush my teeth for two whole minutes.
I put on my comfortable pyjamas.
I can have one story or look at a book in bed.
The lights go off and the room gets dark. I can have my night light on if I like.
I close my eyes and rest. Sleep usually comes after a while. Good night!

templates.title: Going to the Doctor
templates.description: What to expect at the clinic

pages.text: Today I am going to see the doctor.
I will travel to the doctor's surgery with my family.
I will wait in the waiting room. It might be busy.
When it is my turn, someone will call my name or show it on a screen.
The doctor might listen to my chest with a stethoscope. It can feel cold for a moment.
The doctor might give me medicine to help me feel better.
Going to the doctor helps people stay healthy. After the visit, we can go home.
Today I am going to visit the dentist to check my teeth.
I will go to the dentist surgery with my family.
There is a waiting room where people wait until their name is called.
There is a special dentist chair. It can go up and down!
The dentist will shine a light to look at my teeth.
The dentist will check each tooth is healthy and clean.
Looking after my teeth helps keep them healthy. When the check-up is finished, I can go home.
Today I am going to have my flu vaccine. Some people call it a flu jab.
Flu can make people feel poorly in the winter. The vaccine helps my body stay healthy.
I might have my vaccine at school, at the doctor's surgery, or at a pharmacy.
A nurse will give me the vaccine. Nurses give vaccines to lots of children every day.
Most children have the vaccine as a quick spray up the nose. It might feel tickly or cold for a moment.
Some people have a small jab in the arm instead. It might feel like a quick scratch, and it is over very quickly.
I can hold a favourite toy, squeeze someone's hand, or take slow deep breaths while the nurse gives me the vaccine.
Afterwards my nose might be runny, or my arm might feel a bit sore. That is OK. It usually goes away in a day or two.
When it is finished, I have helped keep myself and other people healthy. I can tell my grown-up how it felt.
Today is my first day at my new school.
My grown-up and I can pack my bag the night before.
I will travel to school with my grown-up, or on the bus.
When I arrive, a grown-up from school will be there to welcome me. It is usually my teacher.
There will be a place for me in the classroom. My teacher can show me where it is.
I might meet some new friends today.
Lots of children feel nervous, excited, or both on their first day. That is OK. I can ask my teacher for help.
At the end of the day, my grown-up will pick me up. I can tell them about my day if I want to.
Halloween is on the 31st of October. Lots of people dress up and have fun.
Some people wear costumes and masks. They might look scary or silly, but underneath it is just a person dressed up.
I can choose a costume if I want to. If it feels itchy or too tight, I can tell my grown-up. I can also choose not to wear one.
When we go trick or treating, my grown-up stays with me. We usually only knock at houses with a pumpkin or decorations outside.
I can knock on the door or ring the bell. When the door opens, I can say 'trick or treat!'
The person might offer me some sweets. I usually take one or two and say 'thank you'.
It might be dark and noisy outside. There might be fireworks too. I can wear ear defenders, or tell my grown-up if I need a break.
When we get home, my grown-up will check my sweets before I eat them.
Halloween only happens once a year. When it is over, I can tell my grown-up what I enjoyed.
Christmas is a special time in December. Lots of people celebrate it with their families.
Before Christmas, people put up decorations like a Christmas tree and twinkly lights. Our home might look different for a while. That is OK.
I might see Father Christmas at the shops or at school. He is a person dressed in a red suit. I can say hello, or wave from further away.
On Christmas Day, I might get some presents. They are wrapped in paper, so I won't know what is inside until I open them.
Sometimes I might get a present I wasn't expecting. I can say 'thank you' to the person who gave it to me.
Family or friends might come to visit. The house might be busier and louder than usual. If I need a quiet break, I can tell my grown-up.
We might have a big Christmas dinner with some new foods. I can try a little, or eat the foods I like.
Christmas crackers make a loud bang when they are pulled. I can cover my ears, or watch from further away.
After Christmas, the decorations are put away and things go back to normal. I can tell my grown-up what I enjoyed.
